from __future__ import annotations
import os
import shutil
import subprocess
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import biotite.structure.io as strucio

from pinder.core.utils import setup_logger

log = setup_logger(__name__)


def frodock(
    results_dir: Path,
    n_solutions: int,
    mpi_np: int,
    complex_id: str,
    complex_kind: str,
    complex_receptor: Path,
    complex_ligand: Path,
) -> None:
    """
    Run FroDock on a single receptor-ligand complex and generate `n_solutions` docking solutions.
    Assume that all paths provided are local and all the files exist.
    Assume that `frodock` binary is available in PATH.
    Save results to the specified `results_dir`. Directory will be created if needed.

    Parameters
    ----------
    results_dir : Path
        Path to the docking dataset.
        Resulting path will be `{results_dir}/frodock/{complex_id}/{complex_kind}_decoys/model_{i}.pdb`
    n_solutions : int
        Number of solutions `i = {1..n_solutions}` to generate.
    mpi_np : int
        Number of processors to use for MPI. Default is 8.
    complex_id : str
        PINDER ID of the complex.
    complex_kind : str
        `holo`, `apo` or `predicted`.
    complex_receptor : Path
        All structures are expected to be pre-transformed and ready for docking.
    complex_ligand : Path
        All structures are expected to be pre-transformed and ready for docking.

    """
    log.info(
        f"Running FroDock ({n_solutions} solutions) on complex {complex_id} {complex_kind} {complex_receptor} {complex_ligand}"
    )

    current_dir = os.getcwd()
    output_dir = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp())
    log.info("OUT", output_dir)
    os.chdir(output_dir)

    mpi_path = shutil.which("mpirun")
    dock_path = shutil.which("frodock_mpi_gcc")
    if not dock_path:
        log.error("FroDock binary not found on $PATH!")
        # restore CWD
        os.chdir(current_dir)
        return
    if not mpi_path:
        log.error("mpirun binary not found on $PATH!")
        # restore CWD
        os.chdir(current_dir)
        return

    # file prefices
    R_file_name = complex_receptor.name
    L_file_name = complex_ligand.name

    receptor = R_file_name.split(".")[0]
    ligand = L_file_name.split(".")[0]

    # FRODOCK binaries
    # allow to run MPI as root
    os.environ["OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT"] = "1"
    os.environ["OMPI_ALLOW_RUN_AS_ROOT_CONFIRM"] = "1"
    # --use-hwthread-cpus solves "There are not enough slots available in the system ..." error
    # mpi_np = 45
    run = f"mpirun -np {mpi_np} --use-hwthread-cpus "
    frodock_bin_dir = Path(dock_path).parent
    pre = frodock_bin_dir
    suff = "_mpi_gcc"
    suff2 = "_gcc"
    # Define the stages
    stages = [
        (
            "STAGE-1 Creation of receptor vdw potential map",
            f"{run} {pre}frodockgrid{suff} {receptor}.pdb -o {receptor}_W.mrc",
        ),
        (
            "STAGE-2 Creation of the receptor electrostatic potential map",
            f"{run} {pre}frodockgrid{suff} {receptor}.pdb -o {receptor}_E.mrc -m 1 -t A",
        ),
        (
            "STAGE-3 Creation of the receptor desolvation potential map",
            f"{run} {pre}frodockgrid{suff} {receptor}.pdb -o {receptor}_DS.mrc -m 3",
        ),
        (
            "STAGE-4 Creation of the ligand desolvation potential map",
            f"{run} {pre}frodockgrid{suff} {ligand}.pdb -o {ligand}_DS.mrc -m 3",
        ),
        (
            "STAGE-5 Performing the docking",
            f"{run} {pre}frodock{suff} {receptor}_ASA.pdb {ligand}_ASA.pdb -w {receptor}_W.mrc -e {receptor}_E.mrc --th 10 -d {receptor}_DS.mrc,{ligand}_DS.mrc -t A -o dock.dat -s {pre}soap.bin",
        ),
        (
            "STAGE-6 Clustering and visualization of predictions",
            f"{pre}frodockcluster{suff2} dock.dat {ligand}.pdb --nc {n_solutions} -o clust_dock.dat",
        ),
        (
            f"STAGE-7 Visualize the first {n_solutions} solutions",
            f"{pre}frodockview{suff2} clust_dock.dat -r 1-{n_solutions}",
        ),
        (
            f"STAGE-8 Coordinate generation of the {n_solutions} best predicted solutions",
            f"{pre}frodockview{suff2} clust_dock.dat -r 1-{n_solutions} -p {ligand}.pdb",
        ),
    ]

    # Execute the stages sequentially
    for stage_name, cmd in stages:
        log.debug(stage_name)
        log.debug(cmd)
        try:
            subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True)
            # optionally redirect stderr to stdout
            # subprocess.run(cmd, shell=True, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT)
        except Exception as e:
            log.error(f"ERROR while running stage {stage_name} on {complex_id}: {e}")
            os.chdir(current_dir)
            return

    # normalize the results by renaming the top solutions
    solutions_exist = False
    # docked ligand file exists but we need a complete pose
    receptor_array = strucio.load_structure(f"{receptor}.pdb")
    for i in range(1, n_solutions + 1):
        ligand_file = Path(f"{ligand}_{i}.pdb")
        if ligand_file.exists():
            pose_file = Path(f"{receptor}_{ligand}_{i}.pdb")
            if not pose_file.exists():
                ligand_array = strucio.load_structure(str(ligand_file))
                pose_array = receptor_array + ligand_array
                strucio.save_structure(str(pose_file), pose_array)
            if pose_file.exists():
                solutions_exist = True
                os.rename(pose_file, f"model_{i}.pdb")

    if not solutions_exist:
        log.info(f"ERROR: {complex_kind} {complex_id} did not finish successfully")
        os.chdir(current_dir)
        return

    # delete extra files
    for fname in Path(".").glob("*.pdb"):
        if "model_" not in fname.name:
            fname.unlink()

    # change back to original working directory
    os.chdir(current_dir)

    # copy the results
    results_path_complete = results_dir / f"frodock/{complex_id}/{complex_kind}_decoys/"
    log.info(f"Copying the results to {results_path_complete}")
    results_path_complete.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    shutil.copy(str(output_dir) + "/*.pdb", results_path_complete)


def predict_frodock(
    complex_config: dict[str, str | Path], params: dict[str, Any]
) -> None:
    """
    Run FroDock on a single receptor-ligand complex and generate `n_solutions` docking solutions.
    Assume that all the specified paths are local and the files exist.
    Save results to the specified `results_dir`. Directory is created if needed.

    Parameters
    ----------
    complex_config : dict[str, str | Path]
        Dictionary containing configuration for the complex.

        id : str
            PINDER ID of the complex.
        kind : str
            `holo`, `apo` or `predicted`.
        receptor : Path
            All structures are expected to be pre-transformed and ready for docking.
        ligand : Path
            All structures are expected to be pre-transformed and ready for docking.
    params : dict[str, Any]
        Dictionary containing additional parameters.

        results_dir : Path
            Path to the docking dataset.
            Resulting path will be: `{results_dir}/frodock/{id}/{kind}_decoys/model_{i}.pdb`.
        n_solutions : int
            Number of solutions `i = {1..n_solutions}` to generate.
        mpi_np : int
            Number of processors to use for MPI. Default is 8.
        force : bool
            Force re-running the docking even if the results already exist.
    """
    complex_id = str(complex_config["id"])
    complex_kind = str(complex_config["kind"])
    complex_receptor = Path(complex_config["receptor"])
    complex_ligand = Path(complex_config["ligand"])
    results_dir = Path(params["results_dir"])
    n_solutions = int(params["n_solutions"])
    mpi_np = int(params.get("mpi_np", 8))
    force = bool(params["force"])

    results_path_complete = results_dir / f"frodock/{complex_id}/{complex_kind}_decoys/"
    if not force and (results_path_complete / "model_1.pdb").exists():
        log.info(
            f"Skipping {complex_id} {complex_kind} because it already exists in {results_path_complete}"
        )
        return

    frodock(
        results_dir,
        n_solutions,
        mpi_np,
        complex_id,
        complex_kind,
        complex_receptor,
        complex_ligand,
    )

Never add repositories, keys or source lines, and never enable a commented or disabled source. Setup prints each package it installs and its installed version (`dpkg-query -W <package>`). Run evidence (blind-01 run6, 2026-10-31): setup failed three times on a missing runtime library packaged in the Ubuntu archive (universe); the rule then allowed apt only from the CUDA/NVIDIA lines in `apt_sources`, so neither repair could install it.

## A/harness/ (written by the harness agent or copied from a previous run)
- Optional `args.harness_from` is a non-empty directory path to a previous run's `A/harness/`, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory. After a successful fresh box probe, the pipeline copies the exact bytes of `setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh` and `run_command.sh` into the current `A/harness/` and skips the initial harness agent call. If present, `run_evaluation.sh` is copied too. Missing or unreadable required scripts, or an invalid argument, fail reproduce with `error_class: parse`; there is no fallback harness generation. Without this argument, harness generation is unchanged.
- Reuse writes script-owned `C/harness_source.json` as `{source, files}`. `source` is the absolute source harness directory; `files` maps each copied filename to `{sha256, modified}`. `sha256` is the lowercase 64-digit SHA-256 of the exact original copied bytes and remains unchanged after repair. `modified` starts false and becomes true after an accepted repair of that script, before its upload/rerun, even if that rerun fails. Reuse permits the same bounded setup and anchor repairs (at most four for setup, two for anchors) as generated harnesses; every repair receives the fresh probe. Reuse adds no stage facts and does not reuse probe results, measurements, or stock verification.
- `setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh`, `run_command.sh` are bash scripts. The pipeline invokes them as `bash harness/<name>` from one fresh `/tmp/m5-<uuid>` directory on the already-running operator-managed box. They share that directory across reproduce and profile. No dev lifecycle commands are issued. `BOX` and `FETCH` are inherited unchanged by `boxrun.sh`, including injected executables.
- Harness uploads (the initial upload of every harness script, and the re-upload of rewritten scripts after each accepted repair) use the implement upload encoding, so no process argument or remote command line grows with script size. For each script, the upload truncates `harness/<name>` (`: > harness/<name>`) and then appends its base64 in independently decodable chunks of at most 24,576 characters (`printf %s <chunk> | base64 -d >> harness/<name>`); an empty script is created empty. These lines are batched in order into boxrun commands below 32,768 characters. Every batch begins with `set -e` and `mkdir -p harness out`, runs as operation `upload` under the setup budget, and has its own receipt. A batch that fails (nonzero exit, failed fetch, missing receipt, or a timeout after its identical retry) ends the upload: later batches are not sent and the harness script does not run, and the step fails as a failed upload does today (`infra`, or `timeout` on a timeout). After all batches succeed, the uploaded files are byte-identical to the local harness files. A harness small enough for one batch uploads in exactly one `upload` command, as before. Run evidence (blind-01 run5, 2026-10-31): the single upload command exceeded the operating system's 131,072-byte limit on one argument, spawning boxrun failed with E2BIG before any receipt was written, and reproduce stopped with `infra` before setup ran.
- `setup.sh` installs/builds the exact published baseline in the stock image; sudo is allowed only for apt. Published source/configuration stays under `baseline-published/`; inputs stay under `data/`. Setup builds and checks only the baseline; the fixed pipeline profiler owns profiling tools and installation. Setup must tolerate one retry in the same directory. Tuning is deferred.
- `run_anchors.sh` runs the published protocol at the intake's representative scale and writes `out/anchors_measured.json` as an object mapping each intake item ID (anchors and references) to a finite measured number; with an empty anchors.json it still runs the published command and writes `{}`. Missing or non-numeric measurements fail the corresponding anchor; booleans and nonfinite values count as non-numeric. Additional measurements are ignored for scoring.
- `run_command.sh` contains only the exact measured baseline command and complete environment at the representative scale, including working directory, arguments, CUDA visibility and GPU count. It runs the published binary, saves its output for anchor parsing, and propagates its exit status. `run_anchors.sh` invokes `bash harness/run_command.sh` from the shared working directory without overriding its environment or duplicating the command. Profiling invokes that same file from that same directory. No agent writes profiling scripts or profile outputs.
- `run_command.sh` uses paths relative to its working directory, never absolute paths into the run directory, and writes only under `out/` or temporary files. The concurrency probe and evaluation run it from sibling work directories that link the same trees (see Concurrency probe). Harness and repair prompts state this requirement.
- Optional unit files (U50): `run_units.sh` and `units.json`, used only by the unit equivalence check (U51) and the unit-mode concurrency probe. `units.json` is exactly `{"units": [...]}` with at least four entries, in the order the published full run processes them, each exactly `{id, outputs, cost_s}`: `id` is a unique string matching `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._:+=-]{0,127}$` that identifies that unit to `run_units.sh`; `outputs` is a non-empty array of unique relative paths naming that unit's result files under `out/`, each one or more `/`-separated components made of `[A-Za-z0-9._+=-]`, none of them `.` or `..`; `cost_s` is a finite positive number, the unit's own seconds as recorded in the reproduce run's logs or outputs. `bash harness/run_units.sh <id>...` runs the exact measured command of `run_command.sh` (same binary, configuration, environment and scale) restricted to the listed units (one or more), in the order given, by one of two means: the published program's own subset selection when it takes effect, or otherwise a restricted copy of the prepared input list that the measured command reads, holding only the listed units' original records copied byte for byte in the list's own format, written under `out/` or a temporary directory and passed through an argument, configuration value or environment variable the measured command already accepts. Either way it retains the measured baseline's per-unit code, parameters and inputs exactly as `run_command.sh` runs them, including any documented setup or anchors repairs the measured baseline already carries: the reference is the measured baseline, not the pristine upstream program, and no new code change is allowed. A path-rule conflict that `run_command.sh` already has is inherited and recorded separately; the unit files add none. Reader evidence (run10_diff, 2026-11-01): the entry point's command-line selector exists but has no effect; the measured command reads a prepared input list whose path it already accepts, a restricted list of original records under `out/` adds no write elsewhere, and the per-unit code differences earlier subsetting attempts were flagged for are inherited repairs. Owner decision 2026-11-01: allow selection of original prepared input records while retaining the measured baseline's per-unit code, parameters and inputs. It obeys every `run_command.sh` rule (relative paths, writes only under `out/` or temporary files, no `CUDA_MPS_*` changes), writes each listed unit's `outputs` under `out/` at the same paths as the full run, and propagates the exit status. Under `args.harness_from`, each of the two files present in the source is copied with its exact bytes and recorded in `C/harness_source.json` like the scripts. Files present in `A/harness/` are uploaded with the initial harness upload (same encoding and batching), never later. No repair changes them: after every setup or anchors repair the pipeline restores their bytes (or their absence), as it restores `run_evaluation.sh`. The harness agent is not asked to write them; fresh harness generation is unchanged. The unit equivalence check (U51) and the probe's comparison with the frozen baseline outputs (see Concurrency probe) are their validation.
- The pipeline owns CUDA MPS. No harness script (`setup.sh`, `run_anchors.sh`, `run_command.sh`, `run_evaluation.sh`) may set, unset or override any `CUDA_MPS_*` environment variable, or start or stop an MPS daemon; the scripts inherit these variables unchanged. Harness and repair prompts state this rule. (Method code written in implement is not a harness script and may manage MPS itself.)
- Harness prompts require the published build and binary to run and measurements to come from their OUTPUT. Scripts must never parse or assert on source text. Measurement checks fail only on missing or invalid output; deterministic scoring owns anchor comparisons.
- Without `args.harness_from`, there is one initial agent call (`harness`, `ls-writer`, `sonnet`). Setup permits up to four repairs (`harness-repair`) and anchors up to two (`anchors-repair`) after a nonzero exit, with the same role/model. Each repair receives the failure class and at most the last 200 log lines of the latest failed attempt, and its prompt states its attempt number and the step's limit (`repair attempt <n> of <limit>`). Each later repair runs only after the previous repaired script ran and failed again (nonzero exit or output-gate error); a declined (null) repair, an infrastructure or fetch failure, or a failed upload ends the step. Owner direction 2026-10-30: finish experiments rather than stop them on a fixable failure; a blind run spent its one setup repair on a build-dependency failure, the repair worked, and setup then failed on a different import error that a single repair could not reach. U46 run evidence (blind-01 run7, 2026-10-31): setup spent both of its two repairs on successive script errors; each repair's log tail held its error, each repair targeted it and none regressed, a static check before upload would have caught none, and setup reruns reuse the materials already fetched and verified, so an attempt after a repair costs tens of seconds; an authorized reader judged more repairs of the same kind the smallest sufficient fix. Anchors keep two repairs until a run shows otherwise. The setup repair may rewrite only `setup.sh`. The anchors step executes `run_anchors.sh` and the `run_command.sh` it invokes, so the anchors repair may rewrite either or both and nothing else; a rewritten `run_command.sh` still obeys every `run_command.sh` rule above, and the anchors repair prompt states this. After each repair every rewritten script is recopied, then the step reruns once, with its budget resolved at the rerun's start (U47). Under reuse, an accepted anchors repair marks `modified` true for each of the two scripts whose bytes it changed. Infrastructure/fetch failures do not trigger repairs. Timeouts use the same repairs (the step's own limit), never an extra one. Repair prompts include budget seconds, measured wall seconds and max(0, wall_s-budget_s) overrun seconds. Profiling has no agent repair or execution retry; output/gate failures stop downstream work.

## A/results/reproduce/ and deterministic anchor scoring
- Every reproduce box command fetches remote `out/` into `A/results/reproduce/out/`, and its `<receipt-id>.log` into `A/results/reproduce/`. Logs remain in the agent view. The local fetched `out/` is cleared before each command to prevent stale measurements. The final copy contains the anchor run's outputs. When reproduce passes, the pipeline freezes those outputs on the box: through boxrun, as operation `reproduce-freeze` under the `setup` budget, it runs `test ! -e reproduce-out` and then `cp -a out reproduce-out` in the shared run directory. Like every reproduce command, its fetch replaces `A/results/reproduce/out/`, so that local copy and remote `reproduce-out/` hold the same outputs: the baseline outputs the seal and the test author read. Later stages never write to `reproduce-out/`; remote `out/` after reproduce also collects profiler and probe outputs and further runs of the baseline command, which are not baseline outputs. A failed `reproduce-freeze` (nonzero exit, failed fetch, or timeout) fails reproduce with `error_class: infra`, or `timeout` on a timeout, without repair.
- `python3 m5/score_anchors.py <anchors.json> <measured.json> <out.json>` writes an atomic JSON object with exact keys `anchors`, `anchors_passed`, `anchors_total`, `all_passed`, `references_total`.
  - `anchors` preserves intake order and contains `{id, kind, published_value, measured_value, tolerance, passed}` for every item, with `kind` `"anchor"` or `"reference"`. Items with `uncertainty` keep it unchanged in their row. Reference rows have `passed: null` and `difference` (measured minus published, or null when unmeasured); an unmeasured reference row has `reason` `missing` or `non_numeric` and is never a failure. `tolerance` preserves its input form; `passed` is boolean. Missing or non-numeric measurements are represented by `measured_value: null`. Failed rows additionally contain `reason`: `unknown_comparison`, `missing`, `non_numeric`, `out_of_tolerance` (for `"=="`), or `threshold_not_met` (for inequalities). Unknown comparisons take precedence over measurement failures; missing measurements take precedence over non-numeric measurements. Passing rows have no `reason` field.
  - `anchors_passed` and `anchors_total` count anchors only and `references_total` counts references; all are nonnegative integers. `all_passed` is true exactly when every anchor passed, including when there are none. An empty array is valid. Duplicate IDs, invalid published values, invalid tolerances or uncertainties, and nonfinite calculated equality differences/tolerances are parse errors. Unknown comparisons and missing/non-numeric measurements are anchor failures rather than parse errors.
  - Exit 0 means every anchor passed; exit 4 means at least one anchor failed; exit 1 means invalid/missing input or an output write failure. Invalid input does not produce a new score file. Diagnostics contain no input content.
- The pipeline writes the score to `A/results/reproduce/anchors_scored.json`.
- Reproduce facts are `{anchors_passed, anchors_total, stock_verified, tuned_control_valid}` plus common `tokens_known` and `gpu_busy_known`. Counts remain null until scoring succeeds; `stock_verified` is true only after setup exits 0; `tuned_control_valid` remains null. The gate passes only when stock is verified and every anchor passes (true with no anchors). `run_valid` is true/false when anchor scoring passes/fails with at least one anchor, and null when there are no anchors.

## Unit equivalence check (U51)
- Purpose: before any spend on concurrency, test whether `run_units.sh` reproduces the measured baseline's own per-unit result files, at the earliest point a run can (about one hour after the box starts instead of after reproduce and profile). Owner direction 2026-11-01: test equivalence before spending on concurrency; keep a failed comparison as recorded and never change its criterion after observing it; distinguish ordinary run-to-run variability from an effect of subsetting. The comparison is against a recorded measured baseline, with that baseline's existing limits.
- Optional `args.units_check` is an object with exactly the key `reference`: a non-empty path, resolved relative to the pipeline working directory, to a local directory of a previous run's recorded baseline outputs (its `A/results/reproduce/out/`). An invalid value fails reproduce with `error_class: parse` before any box command. Without `args.units_check`, reproduce and every later stage are unchanged.
- In units-check mode reproduce runs the box probe, harness copy or generation, upload and setup with its repairs exactly as usual. After the harness copy, `A/harness/` must hold `run_units.sh` and a `units.json` valid as defined under "A/harness/" with at least four units; otherwise reproduce fails with `error_class: parse` before the harness upload. After setup passes, the check runs in place of the usual anchors step:
  1. Sample: the four units chosen by the unit-mode sample rule (see Concurrency probe), in sample order.
  2. Subset run: through boxrun, as operation `units-check` under the resolved `anchors` budget, from the shared run directory, one command that removes any earlier `units-check/` and `out/units-check/`; builds a fresh `units-check/` work directory holding a symlink to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work`, `evaluation-work` and `units-check`, plus an empty `out/`; runs `bash harness/run_units.sh <id0> <id1> <id2> <id3>` there with stdout and stderr in `out/units-check/run.log` of the shared run directory; writes the invocation's own monotonic wall seconds to `out/units-check/wall.json` as `{"wall_s": <seconds>}`; copies the work directory's `out/` contents to `out/units-check/files/`, also when the invocation failed; and exits with the invocation's exit status. The command is authored work: no repair and no identical retry. A timeout or infrastructure failure fails reproduce with `timeout` or `infra` as usual.
  3. Comparison, local, before any later reproduce command: the fetched `out/units-check/` is copied to `A/results/reproduce/units-check/`. For every output path of every sample unit, the file under `A/results/reproduce/units-check/files/` must be byte-identical to the same path under `reference`; a file missing on either side is a mismatch. `subset_match` is true exactly when the invocation exited 0 and every file matched.
  4. Variability control: only when the invocation exited 0 and `subset_match` is false, the usual anchors step then runs once as specified above (`run_anchors.sh` with its repairs and scoring), and afterwards the same sample units' files in the fetched full-run `A/results/reproduce/out/` are compared byte for byte with `reference` (`full_match`) and with the saved subset files (`subset_vs_full_match`). Otherwise the anchors step does not run.
- `A/results/reproduce/units_check.json` is written atomically with exactly `{sample, subset_rc, subset_wall_s, cost_sum_s, cost_ratio, files_total, files_matched, subset_match, full_ran, full_match, subset_vs_full_match}`: `sample` is four rows `{index, cost_s}` (manifest position and recorded cost); `subset_rc` the invocation's integer exit status; `subset_wall_s` from `wall.json`, a finite positive number or null when unavailable; `cost_sum_s` the sum of the sample's `cost_s`; `cost_ratio` = `subset_wall_s / cost_sum_s`, or null; `files_total` and `files_matched` count the sample's output paths and the matches; `subset_match` a boolean; `full_ran` a boolean; `full_match` and `subset_vs_full_match` booleans, or null when the full run did not run or did not exit 0. No unit identifier or output path appears in the file.
- Reproduce facts add optional `units_match` (the file's `subset_match`) and `units_full_match` (its `full_match`), each a boolean or null; both are null outside units-check mode and on SKIPPED/stub records, and records without them stay valid. In units-check mode reproduce never runs `reproduce-freeze`. Its status is PASS once setup passed and `units_check.json` was written, whatever the comparison found; when the variability-control anchors step ran, the status follows the usual anchors rules instead. In units-check mode every stage after reproduce except takeaways is SKIPPED, as after a failed stage.

## A/results/profile/ and A/profile-packet.json
- Profile fetches remote `out/` to `A/results/profile/out/`; logs are `A/results/profile/<receipt-id>.log`. Its inputs are therefore under `A/results/profile/out/profile/`. Remote `out/profile/` is cleared before profiling to prevent stale evidence from passing.
- The pipeline uploads trusted `m5/profile_nsys.sh`, `m5/profile_summarise.py` and the collected probe into remote `profiler/`. Through boxrun, it invokes `bash profiler/profile_nsys.sh harness/run_command.sh out/profile <budget_s>`. The profiler reuses `nsys` from PATH or NVIDIA installation paths. Otherwise it tries `nsight-systems-cli` with apt using only source files listed by the probe, without enabling commented repositories or adding sources. If unavailable, it downloads the official Ubuntu 22.04 amd64 CLI package `NsightSystems-linux-cli-public-2025.3.1.90-3582212.deb` from `https://developer.download.nvidia.com/devtools/repos/ubuntu2204/amd64/` into a temporary directory outside `out/` that is removed after installation (the package never reaches `out/` or fetched results), verifies the SHA-256 pinned in the script, installs with `sudo -n dpkg -i` and runs `sudo -n apt-get -f install -y` for dependencies using the image's existing sources without adding repositories. This fixed profiler installation is an exception to the setup-script installation restrictions above. The profiler prepends the discovered Nsight binary directory to PATH. Missing tools, installation failures and collection/export failures emit `M5_PROFILER_INFRA`, write `out/profile/infra.json`, and exit 2; the pipeline classifies these as `infra` without agent calls.
- Collection uses `nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt --sample=none` around the shared command without modifying its environment. An inner launcher measures only that command with a monotonic clock; installation, profiler finalization and CSV export are excluded. The command's output is preserved in `baseline.log` as well as its own saved logs. Export uses `nsys stats --report cuda_gpu_kern_sum,cuda_gpu_mem_time_sum,cuda_api_sum --format csv`. Raw report, CSV files, tool version, export log, `raw_wall_s.json` and `gpu_util_raw.jsonl` remain in `out/profile/`.
- `python3 m5/profile_summarise.py <out_dir>` deterministically writes the three existing profile files. CSV total time/duration units ns, us/µs, ms and s are converted to seconds. Known Nsight skips for absent kernel/memory/API activity count as zero; missing or malformed reports fail parsing. A report is a known skip when its CSV file carries Nsight's `SKIPPED` line and no header row, or when its CSV file is absent, empty or whitespace-only and `stats.log` in the same directory states that the report does not contain its own activity: `does not contain CUDA kernel data` for `stats_cuda_gpu_kern_sum.csv`, `does not contain GPU memory data` for `stats_cuda_gpu_mem_time_sum.csv`, and `does not contain CUDA trace data` for `stats_cuda_api_sum.csv` (U48). These are Nsight's own wordings; the earlier phrases `CUDA memory data` and `CUDA API data` never occur in Nsight output and no longer count as statements. Nsight Systems 2025 writes an empty file for a skipped report where earlier versions wrote none. An absent, empty or whitespace-only file without that statement for its own activity, and any other missing or malformed report, still fails parsing. Run evidence (blind-01 run9, 2026-11-01): the baseline ran to completion under the profiler with no CUDA activity and no capture problem; Nsight 2025 logged the three skips and wrote three empty summary files, and the summariser failed on a missing CSV header, so profile stopped with `parse` instead of reaching its numeric gate. Replay of the merged U48 summariser on run9's saved files (2026-11-01) still failed: Nsight states the memory and API skips as `GPU memory data` and `CUDA trace data`; with those wordings the summariser exits 0 and the gate reports `numeric` (other host time within 2% of total wall). Five rows are emitted: `kernels` (compute), `memcpy H2D` (transfer), `memcpy D2H` (transfer), `CUDA API host time` (other), and `other host time` (other). GPU seconds retain the raw kernel/transfer sums; host GPU seconds are null. Aggregate CSV reports do not identify critical-path intervals: if the four reported sums exceed measured wall, their wall allocations are scaled proportionally to fit. Other host time is the nonnegative wall remainder. These allocations are an aggregate approximation, not measured exclusive phase durations. No stage timestamps are invented; aggregate rows omit `start_s`, so stage utilisation remains null. No bound uses stage utilisation; same-GPU headroom comes from the concurrency probe.
- `stages.json` is an array of `{stage, wall_s, gpu_s}`, optionally including `kind`: `compute`, `transfer`, or `other`, and `start_s`: finite nonnegative elapsed seconds sharing the telemetry clock. Fixed profiler supplies `kind`; legacy rows without it remain accepted. `stage` is a non-empty string; `wall_s` is finite nonnegative seconds; `gpu_s` is finite nonnegative seconds or null and must be present. Fixed profiler wall allocations sum to measured wall without exceeding it; overlapping aggregate durations use the approximation above. Extra input fields are not copied to the packet. Empty arrays parse but fail the numeric gate.
- `total_wall_s.json` is an object with finite positive numeric `total_wall_s` in seconds. The sum of stage wall times must also be finite.
- `gpu_util.json` is an array of `{t, util}` samples collected with `nvidia-smi` during the measured run. `t` is finite nonnegative elapsed seconds; `util` is a finite GPU utilisation percentage in [0,100]. The fixed sampler records the mean across GPUs returned by nvidia-smi, then the summarizer retains only samples during the shared command and rebases monotonic timestamps to its start. A sample with zero utilisation is valid. Empty arrays parse but fail the numeric gate; missing files or malformed samples fail parsing.
- The deterministic pipeline writes `A/profile-packet.json` with exact keys:
  - `stages`: the validated timing rows, preserving optional `kind`, each augmented with `wall_fraction = min(1, wall_s / total_wall_s)`, `start_s`, and `mean_gpu_util` (fraction in [0,1], or null). When supplied, `start_s` must be measured on the telemetry clock. Legacy rows without `start_s` record null start and utilisation; stage order does not establish a measured telemetry window. Stage endpoints must remain finite. Stage utilisation is the arithmetic mean of telemetry percentages divided by 100 in `[start_s, start_s + wall_s)`; no samples means null. Never substitute GPU busy seconds for utilisation;
  - `total_wall_s`: the measured total;
  - `timed_fraction = min(1, sum(stage.wall_s) / total_wall_s)`;
  - `gpu_telemetry`: true only when the validated `gpu_util.json` array is non-empty; stage `gpu_s` values do not establish telemetry.
  - `gpu_count`: `C/box.json.gpu_count` when nonnegative integer, otherwise count parsed from allocation `type` (`gpu_<N>x_...`), otherwise the collected probe's `nvidia.gpus.length`. Unavailable inventory defaults conservatively to 1; an empty inventory records 0.
  - `concurrency`: the validated `concurrency.json` object (see Concurrency probe), or null when the probe did not run or its output is missing or invalid.
  - `host_only`: boolean (U49). True exactly when the profile shows no CUDA activity: the rows `kernels`, `memcpy H2D`, `memcpy D2H` and `CUDA API host time` are all present, each with `wall_s` 0 and `gpu_s` 0 or null, and `gpu_util.json` holds at least one sample and every sample's `util` is 0. Otherwise false, including for profiles without those rows.
- Profile facts are `{profile_complete, timed_fraction, gpu_telemetry}` plus common `tokens_known` and `gpu_busy_known`, plus optional `headroom`: the packet's `concurrency.factor` (finite positive ratio) or null, and optional `host_only`: the packet's `host_only` boolean, or null when no packet was written. Every executed profile stage emits `headroom` and `host_only`; both are optional in the v2 schema so older records stay valid, and both are null on SKIPPED/stub records. `profile_complete` is true when the command exits 0 and all three inputs validate, even when the numeric gate fails. The deterministic gate requires at least three stages, no process wrappers, `timed_fraction >= 0.9`, and `gpu_telemetry=true`. A stage is a process wrapper if its name contains a case-insensitive token `process`, `wrapper`, `telemetry`, `total`, or `overall` delimited by whitespace, underscores, hyphens, or string boundaries, or if its `wall_s` is within 2% of `total_wall_s` (inclusive). Any wrapper fails the gate, even alongside three internal stages. In a host-only profile (packet `host_only` true) the `other host time` row is exempt from the 2% test, though not from the name test: the fixed profiler computes it as the wall-time remainder, so with no CUDA activity it is the whole command by construction rather than a wrapper around measured stages. Every other gate condition applies to host-only profiles unchanged, and profiles that are not host-only are gated exactly as before. A host-only profile leaves the pipelining and multi-GPU bounds at 1 (no transfer or compute time); its whole-workload bounds come only from the concurrency probe. Run evidence (blind-01 run9, replayed on its saved files 2026-11-01): the published baseline is CPU-only; Nsight recorded no CUDA kernel, memory or API activity, GPU utilisation was zero in every sample, and `other host time` was the whole command, so the 2% test failed the gate as `numeric` and the concurrency probe never ran. Owner decision 2026-11-01: CPU-only baselines are in scope. Numeric gate failures preserve the packet and use `error_class: numeric`; missing or invalid files use `error_class: parse`. A failed gate or parse stops downstream work without a profile repair.

## Concurrency probe: calibration of same-GPU headroom
- Purpose: measure, before any prediction or method exists, how much more throughput one GPU gives when the unchanged published command runs several times at once. This measured factor is the only source of same-GPU headroom for bounds. No model call is involved.
- When the profile command exits 0 and the profile gate passes, the pipeline uploads trusted `m5/concurrency_probe.py` to remote `profiler/` and, through boxrun as operation `concurrency` with the resolved `profile` budget, runs `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py harness/run_command.sh out/concurrency <budget_s>` from the shared run directory. Remote `out/concurrency/` is cleared first. Fetched files land in `A/results/profile/out/concurrency/`; the log is `A/results/profile/<receipt-id>.log`. There is no agent repair and no execution retry. Probe receipts count toward profile v1 `usd` and `gpu_s` like other box receipts.
- Each invocation runs `bash harness/run_command.sh` with its working directory set to a fresh `concurrency-work/<label>/` under the shared run directory. That directory holds a symlink to every top-level entry of the shared run directory except `out`, `profiler`, `concurrency-work` and `evaluation-work`, plus an empty `out/` directory. Labels are `single-1`, `single-2`, `single-3`, `n2-1`, `n2-2`, `n4-1` to `n4-4`. Each invocation's stdout and stderr go to `out/concurrency/logs/<label>.log` of the shared run directory. The environment is inherited unchanged apart from the MPS variables below. Nsight is not used.
- MPS: when `nvidia-cuda-mps-control` is on PATH, the probe starts a user-level daemon (`nvidia-cuda-mps-control -d`) with `CUDA_MPS_PIPE_DIRECTORY` and `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` set to fresh directories under `concurrency-work/`, passes both variables to every invocation, and stops the daemon (`echo quit | nvidia-cuda-mps-control` with the same variables) before exiting, including after failures and on SIGTERM. If the daemon fails to start or any invocation fails under MPS, the probe stops the daemon, records `mps_failed: true`, and repeats the complete probe once without MPS in fresh work directories. Without the binary there is no MPS and `mps_failed` is false.
- MPS use is verified, not assumed. The daemon's `control.log` in its `CUDA_MPS_LOG_DIRECTORY` records each client connection as a line containing `NEW CLIENT <pid> from user <uid>`. After each single run and each batch under MPS, the probe counts these lines (case-sensitive substring `NEW CLIENT `, followed by an integer pid and ` from user `). The count must have grown by at least the number of copies just run (1 for a single run, n for a batch of n). A missing or unreadable log, or a smaller increase, means the copies did not run under MPS: the probe treats this like an invocation failure under MPS (stop the daemon, `mps_failed: true`, repeat the complete probe once without MPS). `mps: true` is therefore recorded only when every counted measurement was verified to run under MPS. No log content enters `concurrency.json`.
- Sequence: three single runs one after another, then 2 copies started together, then 4 copies started together. Wall seconds come from a monotonic clock around each subprocess; a batch's wall runs from launching its first copy to the exit of its last. `T1` is the median of the single walls. A single run that exits nonzero stops the probe with a null factor. Before each batch, the batch is skipped when `n * T1` exceeds `0.9 * budget_s` minus the probe's elapsed seconds. A batch counts only when every copy exits 0. For a counted batch, `factor_n = n * T1 / wall_n`.
- `out/concurrency/concurrency.json` is written atomically with exactly `{mps, mps_failed, single_wall_s, batches, factor}`:
  - `mps`: boolean, true when the recorded measurements ran under MPS; `mps_failed`: boolean;
  - `single_wall_s`: array of exactly three entries, each a finite positive number or null (failed or not run);
  - `batches`: exactly two rows, in order n=2 then n=4, each exactly `{n, wall_s, all_ok, skipped, factor}`; `wall_s` and `factor` are finite positive numbers or null, `all_ok` and `skipped` are booleans, and `factor` is null unless the batch counted;
  - `factor`: the largest counted `factor_n`, or null when any single run failed or no batch counted.
  The probe exits 0 whenever it writes the file, including with a null factor, and 2 when it cannot. It does not check output correctness: it measures throughput only.
- The probe never fails the profile stage and never changes the profile gate. A probe timeout, nonzero exit, or missing or invalid file gives packet `concurrency: null` and `headroom: null`. The pipeline validates the file against the exact shape above before copying it into the packet.
- Unit mode (U50). When the profile gate passes with packet `host_only` true and `A/harness/` holds both `run_units.sh` and `units.json`, the probe runs in unit mode: `python3 -I profiler/concurrency_probe.py --units harness/run_units.sh harness/units.json out/concurrency <budget_s>`, with the same upload, operation, budget, clearing, fetch, log location and no-retry rules as command mode. Otherwise the probe runs in command mode exactly as described above. Unit mode never uses MPS and does not look for the MPS binary. It compares the same four units run in one invocation, as separate invocations one after another, and as separate invocations at once, holding inputs and per-unit configuration fixed and checking every output byte for byte. Owner decision 2026-11-01: the smallest bounded experiment that resolves whether a CPU-only baseline's units gain throughput when run at once, with only the pipeline changes that comparison needs. Reader evidence (blind-01 run9): units are distinct inputs, selectable by restricting the prepared input list to original records (the command-line selector has no effect); each unit writes its own result files at the same paths in full and subset runs, with no run-specific content, and its outputs repeat bit for bit; the reproduce logs record every unit's cost; whether a unit reads state left by earlier units of the same invocation is unknown, which the comparison with the frozen baseline tests; units take 1 to 10 min with a cost spread over 50%; the baseline's own threads already use at least half the logical CPUs. Command mode would instead run three whole commands of 1 to 2 h and compare no outputs.
- Sample: units sorted by `cost_s` ascending, ties by manifest order; the sample is the four consecutive sorted units starting at sorted position floor((N - 4) / 2), N being the number of units, kept in that order as sample positions 0 to 3. Units near the median cost keep concurrent invocations of similar length, so a batch runs at its full width for nearly its whole wall time; the factor therefore describes typical units, not the shortest or longest.
- Arms run in this fixed order, every invocation in a fresh work directory built as in command mode (named `<label>` for an arm with one invocation, `<label>-<j>` for invocation j = 1, 2, ... of an arm with several):
  - `a-1`: one invocation `bash harness/run_units.sh <id0> <id1> <id2> <id3>` (sample order), the baseline's own serial mode;
  - `b-1`: four invocations of one unit each, one after another in sample order;
  - `c2-1`: sample units 0 and 1 started together, then, after both exit, units 2 and 3 started together;
  - `c4-1`: all four started together;
  - `c4-2`, `c2-2`, `b-2`, `a-2`: the same arms again in reverse order, to balance drift.
  Each invocation's stdout and stderr go to `out/concurrency/logs/<work directory name>.log` of the shared run directory, and its environment is inherited unchanged. An arm's wall runs on a monotonic clock from launching its first invocation to the exit of its last.
- Output checks. After `a-1`, every output path of every sample unit under `a-1`'s `out/` must be byte-identical to the same path under the shared run directory's `reproduce-out/` (`baseline_match`); a file missing on either side is a mismatch. When `a-1` exits nonzero or `baseline_match` is false, no later arm runs. After every later invocation, its units' output files must be byte-identical to `a-1`'s (`outputs_match`, true when every later executed invocation matched). An arm counts when all of its invocations exit 0 and all of their compared files match.
- Budget: before each arm, that arm and every later arm are skipped when its estimate exceeds `0.9 * budget_s` minus the probe's elapsed seconds. The estimate is the sum of the sample's `cost_s` for `a-1`, and `a-1`'s measured wall for every later arm.
- Resource use. For each invocation, from `os.wait4` on its process (which includes its waited-for descendants): `cpu_s` (user plus system seconds), `max_rss_kb`, `nivcsw` (involuntary context switches), `inblock` and `oublock`. For each arm, sampled about once a second while it runs: `busy_fraction` (mean non-idle share of total CPU time from `/proc/stat`, idle including iowait), `mem_available_min_kb` (the minimum `MemAvailable` from `/proc/meminfo`) and `threads_max` (the largest sum of `Threads` from `/proc/<pid>/status` over the processes of the arm's invocations; each invocation starts its own session and process group). An arm's `cpu_s` is the sum over its invocations and `effective_cores` is that sum divided by the arm's wall. Memory bandwidth and caches are not measured.
- In unit mode `out/concurrency/concurrency.json` is written atomically with exactly `{mode, mps, mps_failed, outcome, units_total, sample, baseline_match, outputs_match, serial_wall_s, separate_wall_s, batches, arms, nproc, mem_total_kb, factor}`:

def get_pinder_location() -> Path:
    """
    Determines the base directory location for the Pinder data.

    First, check the environment for PINDER_DATA_DIR. If provided, assume
    it is the full path to the directory containing the index, pdbs/, and mappings/.
    Otherwise, the PINDER_BASE_DIR environment variable is checked, and if unset,
    falls back to the default XDG_DATA_HOME location (~/.local/share), and
    appends the current version of the Pinder release. The Pinder release can be
    controlled via the PINDER_RELEASE environment variable.

    Returns:
        Path: The path to the base directory for Pinder data.
    """
    pinder_data = os.environ.get("PINDER_DATA_DIR", "")
    default_loc = os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME", Path.home() / ".local/share")
    if pinder_data:
        pinder_base = Path(pinder_data)
    else:
        base_dir = os.environ.get("PINDER_BASE_DIR", default_loc)
        pinder_release = os.environ.get("PINDER_RELEASE", "2024-02")
        if isinstance(base_dir, str):
            base_dir = Path(base_dir)
        pinder_base = base_dir.absolute() / "pinder" / pinder_release
    if not pinder_base.is_dir():
        pinder_base.mkdir(exist_ok=True, parents=True)
        log.debug(f"Pinder is located at {pinder_base}")
    return pinder_base


def get_pinder_bucket_root() -> str:
    """Constructs the public R2 release URL for the Pinder data
    based on the PINDER_RELEASE environment variable.

    Returns:
        str: The root bucket path as a string.
    """
    pinder_release = os.environ.get("PINDER_RELEASE", "2024-02")
    return str(dataset.release_url(pinder_release))


def get_index_location(
    csv_name: str = "index.parquet", remote: bool = False
) -> Path | str:
    """Gets the file path for the Pinder index CSV/Parquet file, either locally or remotely.

    Parameters:
        csv_name (str): The name of the CSV/Parquet file. Defaults to "index.parquet".
        remote (bool): A flag to determine if the remote file path should be returned.
                       Defaults to False.

    Returns:
        Union[Path, str]:
            The path to the index CSV/Parquet file, either as a Path object (local)
            or a string (remote).
    """
    if remote:
        return f"{get_pinder_bucket_root()}/{csv_name}"
    return get_pinder_location() / csv_name


@lru_cache
def get_index(csv_name: str = "index.parquet", update: bool = False) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Retrieves the Pinder index as a pandas DataFrame. If the index is not already
    loaded, it reads from the local CSV/Parquet file, or downloads it if not present.

    Parameters:
        csv_name (str): The name of the CSV/Parquet file to load. Defaults to "index.parquet".
        update (bool): Whether to force update index on disk even if it exists.
            Default is False.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: The Pinder index as a DataFrame.
    """
    if "/" in str(csv_name):
        # A custom index at a local path or HTTP URL
        custom_index = True
        local_index = get_pinder_location() / "custom_indices" / Path(csv_name).name
        if not local_index.parent.is_dir():
            local_index.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True, parents=True)
    else:
        local_index = Path(get_index_location(csv_name))
        custom_index = False
    if local_index.suffix in [".csv", ".gz"]:
        reader = pd.read_csv
        writer = "to_csv"
        cast_types = True
        # reader_kwargs = {}
    elif local_index.suffix == ".parquet":
        reader = pd.read_parquet
        writer = "to_parquet"
        cast_types = False
        # reader_kwargs = {"engine": "pyarrow"}
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unsupported file type for index: {local_index.suffix}! Use csv or parquet."
        )
    if local_index.is_file() and not update and not custom_index:
        # Only load cached index when update is False and its not a custom index
        pindex = reader(local_index)
    else:
        # Given the potential duplicate named indices, we force-update any custom index
        if custom_index:
            pindex = dataset.read_dataframe(csv_name)
        else:
            pindex = dataset.read_dataframe(get_index_location(csv_name, remote=True))
        getattr(pindex, writer)(local_index, index=False)

    # for backwards compatibility:
    drop_cols = ["affinity_class", "pKd_pKi_pIC50", "tmp_chain2", "pinder_af2_hard"]
    for c in drop_cols:
        if c in pindex.columns:
            pindex.drop(columns=c, inplace=True)

    pindex = fix_index(
        pindex,
        index_fields=list(IndexEntry.__annotations__.keys()),
        cast_types=cast_types,
    )
    return pindex


@lru_cache
def get_metadata(
    csv_name: str = "metadata.parquet",
    update: bool = False,
    extra_glob: str = "metadata-*.csv.gz",
    extra_data: SupplementaryData | tuple[SupplementaryData] | tuple[()] = (),
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Retrieves the Pinder index metadata as a pandas DataFrame.

    If the metadata is not already loaded, it reads from the local CSV/Parquet file,
    or downloads it if not present.

    Also attempts to read extra metadata. We assume that all extra CSV
    files contain an `id` field.

    Parameters:
        csv_name (str): The name of the CSV file to load. Defaults to "metadata.parquet".
        update (bool): Whether to force update index on disk even if it exists. Default is False.
        extra_glob (str): The pattern to match extra metadata CSV files. Defaults to "metadata-\*.csv.gz"

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: The Pinder metadata as a DataFrame.

    """
    local_metadata = Path(get_index_location(csv_name))
    if local_metadata.suffix in [".csv", ".gz"]:
        reader = pd.read_csv
        writer = "to_csv"
        cast_types = True
        # reader_kwargs = {}
    elif local_metadata.suffix == ".parquet":
        reader = pd.read_parquet
        writer = "to_parquet"
        cast_types = False
        # reader_kwargs = {"engine": "pyarrow"}
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unsupported file type for metadata: {local_metadata.suffix}! Use csv or parquet."
        )
    if local_metadata.is_file() and not update:
        metadata = reader(local_metadata)
    else:
        metadata = dataset.read_dataframe(get_index_location(csv_name, remote=True))
        getattr(metadata, writer)(local_metadata, index=False)

    # Backwards compatibility with old column names
    meta_cols = set(metadata.columns)
    if (
        len(
            {"number_of_components_1", "number_of_components_2"}.intersection(meta_cols)
        )
        != 2
    ):
        metadata.rename(
            {
                "number_of_components1": "number_of_components_1",
                "number_of_components2": "number_of_components_2",
            },
            axis=1,
            inplace=True,
        )
    if len({"length_resolved_1", "length_resolved_2"}.intersection(meta_cols)) != 2:
        metadata.loc[:, "length_resolved_1"] = metadata.length1
        metadata.loc[:, "length_resolved_2"] = metadata.length2

    metadata = fix_metadata(
        metadata,
        metadata_fields=list(MetadataEntry.__annotations__.keys()),
        cast_types=cast_types,
    )

    # Try to get extra metadata, if it exists
    if not isinstance(extra_data, tuple):
        extra_data = (extra_data,)
    extra_metadata = get_extra_metadata(
        get_pinder_location(),
        get_pinder_bucket_root(),
        glob_pattern=extra_glob,
        update=update,
        extra_data=extra_data,
    )
    if extra_metadata is not None and not extra_metadata.empty:
        # Only keep non-common columns + id column to merge on to prevent conflicts
        common_cols = set(extra_metadata.columns).intersection(
            set(metadata.columns)
        ) - {"id"}
        if common_cols:
            extra_metadata.drop(columns=list(common_cols), inplace=True)
        metadata = pd.merge(metadata, extra_metadata, on="id", how="left")

    return metadata


@lru_cache
def get_extra_metadata(
    local_location: str,
    remote_location: str,
    glob_pattern: str = "metadata-*.csv.gz",
    extra_data: tuple[SupplementaryData] | tuple[()] = (),
    update: bool = False,
) -> pd.DataFrame | None:
    """Retrieves extra metadata as a pandas DataFrame.

    If the metadata is not already loaded, it reads from local CSV files,
    or downloads them if not present.

    We assume that all CSV files contain an `id` field.

    Parameters:
        local_location (str):
            The filepath to the local directory containing CSV files.
        remote_location (str):
            The filepath to the remote location containing CSV files.
        glob_pattern (str): The pattern to match extra metadata CSV files. Defaults to
            "metadata-\*.csv.gz"
        update (bool): Whether to force update index on disk even if it exists.
            Default is False.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: The Pinder metadata as a DataFrame.
    """
    local_metadata = [p for p in Path(local_location).glob(glob_pattern) if p.is_file()]

    metadata_dfs = []
    if local_metadata and not update:
        metadata_dfs = [pd.read_csv(meta) for meta in local_metadata if meta.is_file()]
    else:
        metadata_dfs = [
            dataset.read_dataframe(meta)
            for meta in dataset.list_files(remote_location)
            if fnmatch(Path(meta).name, glob_pattern)
        ]
    if extra_data:
        for data in extra_data:
            supp = get_supplementary_data(data, update=update)
            metadata_dfs.append(supp)

    if metadata_dfs:
        return reduce(partial(pd.merge, on="id", how="outer"), metadata_dfs)
    else:
        return None

    sequence_database = "sequence_database.parquet"
    supplementary_metadata = "supplementary_metadata.parquet"
    entity_metadata = "entity_metadata.parquet"
    chain_metadata = "chain_metadata.parquet"

    enzyme_classification_metadata = "enzyme_classification_metadata.parquet"

    sabdab_metadata = "sabdab_metadata.parquet"

    paired_neff = "test_split_paired_neffs.parquet"
    transient_interface_metadata = "transient_interface_metadata.parquet"
    ialign_split_similarity_labels = "ialign_split_similarity_labels.parquet"


@lru_cache
def get_supplementary_data(
    supplementary_data: SupplementaryData, update: bool = False
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Retrieves supplementary data file exposed in the Pinder dataset as a pandas DataFrame.
    If the data is not already loaded, it reads from the local Parquet file, or downloads it if not present.

    Parameters:
        supplementary_data (SupplementaryData): The name of the Parquet file to load.
        update (bool): Whether to force update data on disk even if it exists.
            Default is False.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: The requested supplementary Pinder data as a DataFrame.
    """
    if not isinstance(supplementary_data, SupplementaryData):
        supplementary_data = SupplementaryData[supplementary_data]
    local_index = Path(get_index_location(supplementary_data.value))
    if local_index.suffix == ".parquet":
        reader = pd.read_parquet
        writer = "to_parquet"
    else:
        raise ValueError(
            f"Unsupported file type for sequence database: {local_index.suffix}! Use parquet."
        )
    if local_index.is_file() and not update:
        data = reader(local_index)
    else:
        data = dataset.read_dataframe(
            get_index_location(supplementary_data.value, remote=True)
        )
        getattr(data, writer)(local_index, index=False)

    return data


@lru_cache
def get_sequence_database(
    pqt_name: str = "sequence_database.parquet", update: bool = False
) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Retrieves sequences for all PDB files in the Pinder dataset (including dimers, bound and unbound monomers) as a pandas DataFrame.
    If the database is not already loaded, it reads from the local Parquet file, or downloads it if not present.

    Parameters:
        pqt_name (str): The name of the Parquet file to load. Defaults to "sequence_database.parquet".
        update (bool): Whether to force update sequence database on disk even if it exists.
            Default is False.

    Returns:
        pd.DataFrame: The Pinder sequence database as a DataFrame.
    """
    seq_db = get_supplementary_data(SupplementaryData(pqt_name), update=update)
    return seq_db


def download_dataset(skip_inflation: bool = False) -> None:
    """Downloads the Pinder dataset archives (PDBs and mappings) and optionally inflates them.

    Parameters:
        skip_inflation (bool):
            If True, the method will skip inflating (unzipping) the
            downloaded archives. Defaults to False.

    Note:
        Required disk space to download the full Pinder dataset:

        .. code-block:: text

            # compressed archives (decimal GB)
            168.88 GB    pdbs.zip
            0.18 GB      test_set_pdbs.zip
            7.23 GB      mappings.zip

            # complete directories after pinder_sync_data (decimal GB)
            1013.35 GB   pdbs
            0.73 GB      test_set_pdbs
            23.83 GB     mappings

        The archives omit files listed in the release manifests. Run
        ``pinder_sync_data`` after extraction to fetch missing files.
        Existing files are skipped without checksum verification.
        Allow at least 1.2 TB of free disk space for the default
        download-and-sync workflow, including filesystem overhead.

    """
    root = get_pinder_location()
    expected_arch_files: dict[str, int] = {
        "pdbs": pc.PDB_FILE_COUNT,
        "test_set_pdbs": pc.TEST_SET_PDB_FILE_COUNT,
        "mappings": pc.MAPPING_FILE_COUNT,
    }
    remote_archs = []
    local_paths = []
    archive_paths = []
    for arch_name, n_expected in expected_arch_files.items():
        local_dir = root / arch_name
        local_arch = root / f"{arch_name}.zip"
        remote_arch = get_pinder_bucket_root() + f"/{arch_name}.zip"
        if local_dir.is_dir():
            ext = "." + arch_name[0:-1]
            n_existing = len(list(local_dir.glob(ext)))
        else:
            n_existing = 0

        # Only unzip archive if contents are incomplete
        unzip = n_existing < n_expected
        # Only download archive if directory doesn't exist or contents are incomplete
        download = unzip and not local_arch.is_file()
        if download:
            remote_archs.append(remote_arch)
            local_paths.append(local_arch)
        else:
            log.info(f"Archive {local_arch} exists, skipping download...")
        if unzip:
            archive_paths.append(local_arch)
        else:
            log.info(f"Skipping inflation, {local_arch} contents are valid...")

    if remote_archs:
        dataset.download_files(remote_archs, local_paths)

    if skip_inflation:
        return
    for local_arch in archive_paths:
        if local_arch.is_file():
            with ZipFile(local_arch, "r") as archive:
                for member in tqdm(archive.infolist(), desc=f"Extracting {local_arch}"):
                    try:
                        archive.extract(member, local_arch.parent)
                    except zip_error as e:
                        log.error(str(e))
            local_arch.unlink()


def get_arg_parser_args(
    argv: list[str] | None = None,
    title: str = "Download latest pinder dataset to disk",
) -> dict[str, str | bool]:
    """The command-line arg parser for different pinder data downloads and updates.

    It accepts command-line arguments to specify the base directory, release version,
    and whether to skip inflating the compressed archives.

    Parameters:
        argv (Optional[List[str]]): The command-line arguments. If None, sys.argv is used.

    """
    import sys
    from argparse import ArgumentParser

    # Check if XDG_DATA_HOME is defined, if not fallback to expected
    default_loc = os.environ.get("XDG_DATA_HOME", Path.home() / ".local/share")
    # Prefer checking PINDER_BASE_DIR, if not set then use default location
    default_base_dir = os.environ.get("PINDER_BASE_DIR", default_loc)
    parser = ArgumentParser(prog=title)
    parser.add_argument(
        "--pinder_base_dir",
        help="specify a non-default pinder base directory",
        required=False,
        default=default_base_dir,
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--pinder_release",
        help="specify a pinder dataset version",
        required=False,
        default="2024-02",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--skip_inflation",
        help="if passed, will only download the compressed archives without unpacking",
        action="store_true",
        default=False,
    )
    vargs = vars(parser.parse_args(argv if argv is not None else sys.argv[1:]))
    base_dir = str(Path(vargs["pinder_base_dir"]).absolute())
    release = str(vargs["pinder_release"])
    os.environ["PINDER_BASE_DIR"] = base_dir
    os.environ["PINDER_RELEASE"] = release
    log.info(f"Using {base_dir} as base directory for Pinder {release}")
    return vargs


def download_pinder_cmd(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    """The command-line interface for downloading the latest Pinder dataset to disk.

    It accepts command-line arguments to specify the base directory, release version,
    and whether to skip inflating the compressed archives.

    Parameters:
        argv (Optional[List[str]]): The command-line arguments. If None, sys.argv is used.

    Note:
        Required disk space to download the full Pinder dataset:

        .. code-block:: text

            # compressed archives (decimal GB)
            168.88 GB    pdbs.zip
            0.18 GB      test_set_pdbs.zip
            7.23 GB      mappings.zip

            # complete directories after pinder_sync_data (decimal GB)
            1013.35 GB   pdbs
            0.73 GB      test_set_pdbs
            23.83 GB     mappings

        The archives omit files listed in the release manifests. Run
        ``pinder_sync_data`` after extraction to fetch missing files.
        Existing files are skipped without checksum verification.
        Allow at least 1.2 TB of free disk space for the default
        download-and-sync workflow, including filesystem overhead.

    """
    vargs = get_arg_parser_args(argv)
    skip_inflation = bool(vargs.pop("skip_inflation", False))
    download_dataset(skip_inflation=skip_inflation)


def update_index_cmd(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    """The command-line interface for downloading the latest Pinder index to disk.

    It accepts command-line arguments to specify the base directory and release version.

    Parameters:
        argv (Optional[List[str]]): The command-line arguments. If None, sys.argv is used.

    """

    vargs = get_arg_parser_args(argv, "Download latest pinder index to disk")
    get_index(update=True)
    get_metadata(update=True)


def get_missing_blobs(prefix: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[Path]]:
    local_dir = get_pinder_location() / prefix
    local_names = (
        {path.name for path in local_dir.iterdir() if path.is_file()}
        if local_dir.is_dir()
        else set()
    )
    remote = [
        uri
        for uri in dataset.list_files(get_pinder_bucket_root(), prefix)
        if Path(uri).name not in local_names
    ]
    return remote, [local_dir / Path(uri).name for uri in remote]


def sync_pinder_structure_data(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> None:
    """The command-line interface for syncing any structural data files missing on disk.

    It accepts command-line arguments to specify the base directory and release version.

    Parameters:
        argv (Optional[List[str]]): The command-line arguments. If None, sys.argv is used.

    """

    get_arg_parser_args(argv, "Sync missing pinder structural data files to disk")
    for prefix in ["pdbs", "test_set_pdbs", "mappings"]:
        dataset.sync_directory(
            get_pinder_bucket_root(), prefix, get_pinder_location() / prefix
        )


class IndexEntry(BaseModel):
    """Pydantic model representing a single entry in the Pinder index.

    Stores all associated metadata for a particular dataset entry as attributes.

    Parameters
    ----------
        split (str):
            The type of data split (e.g., 'train', 'test').
        id (str):
            The unique identifier for the dataset entry.
        pdb_id (str):
            The PDB identifier associated with the entry.
        cluster_id (str):
            The cluster identifier associated with the entry.
        cluster_id_R (str):
            The cluster identifier associated with receptor dimer body.
        cluster_id_L (str):
            The cluster identifier associated with ligand dimer body.
        pinder_s (bool):
            Flag indicating if the entry is part of the Pinder-S dataset.
        pinder_xl (bool):
            Flag indicating if the entry is part of the Pinder-XL dataset.
        pinder_af2 (bool):
            Flag indicating if the entry is part of the Pinder-AF2 dataset.
        uniprot_R (str):
            The UniProt identifier for the receptor protein.
        uniprot_L (str):
            The UniProt identifier for the ligand protein.
        holo_R_pdb (str):
            The PDB identifier for the holo form of the receptor protein.
        holo_L_pdb (str):
            The PDB identifier for the holo form of the ligand protein.
        predicted_R_pdb (str):
            The PDB identifier for the predicted structure of the receptor protein.
        predicted_L_pdb (str):
            The PDB identifier for the predicted structure of the ligand protein.
        apo_R_pdb (str):
            The PDB identifier for the apo form of the receptor protein.
        apo_L_pdb (str):
            The PDB identifier for the apo form of the ligand protein.
        apo_R_pdbs (str):
            The PDB identifiers for the apo forms of the receptor protein.
        apo_L_pdbs (str):
            The PDB identifiers for the apo forms of the ligand protein.
        holo_R (bool):
            Flag indicating if the holo form of the receptor protein is available.
        holo_L (bool):
            Flag indicating if the holo form of the ligand protein is available.
        predicted_R (bool):
            Flag indicating if the predicted structure of the receptor protein is available.
        predicted_L (bool):
            Flag indicating if the predicted structure of the ligand protein is available.
        apo_R (bool):
            Flag indicating if the apo form of the receptor protein is available.
        apo_L (bool):
            Flag indicating if the apo form of the ligand protein is available.
        apo_R_quality (str):
            Classification of apo receptor pairing quality. Can be `high, low, ''`.
            All test and val are labeled high. Train split is broken into `high` and `low`,
            depending on whether the pairing was produced with a low-confidence quality/eval metrics
            or `high` if the same metrics were used as for train and val.
            If no pairing exists, it is labeled with an empty string.
        apo_L_quality (str):
            Classification of apo ligand pairing quality. Can be `high, low, ''`.
            All test and val are labeled high. Train split is broken into `high` and `low`,
            depending on whether the pairing was produced with a low-confidence quality/eval metrics
            or `high` if the same metrics were used as for train and val.
            If no pairing exists, it is labeled with an empty string.
        chain1_neff (float):
            The Neff value for the first chain in the protein complex.
        chain2_neff (float):
            The Neff value for the second chain in the protein complex.
        chain_R (str):
            The chain identifier for the receptor protein.
        chain_L (str):
            The chain identifier for the ligand protein.
        contains_antibody (bool):
            Flag indicating if the protein complex contains an antibody as per SAbDab.
        contains_antigen (bool):
            Flag indicating if the protein complex contains an antigen as per SAbDab.
        contains_enzyme (bool):
            Flag indicating if the protein complex contains an enzyme as per EC ID number.
    """

    model_config = ConfigDict(extra="forbid")

    split: str
    id: str
    pdb_id: str
    cluster_id: str
    cluster_id_R: str
    cluster_id_L: str
    pinder_s: bool
    pinder_xl: bool
    pinder_af2: bool
    uniprot_R: str
    uniprot_L: str
    holo_R_pdb: str
    holo_L_pdb: str
    predicted_R_pdb: str
    predicted_L_pdb: str
    apo_R_pdb: str
    apo_L_pdb: str
    apo_R_pdbs: str
    apo_L_pdbs: str
    holo_R: bool
    holo_L: bool
    predicted_R: bool
    predicted_L: bool
    apo_R: bool
    apo_L: bool
    apo_R_quality: str
    apo_L_quality: str
    chain1_neff: float
    chain2_neff: float
    chain_R: str
    chain_L: str
    contains_antibody: bool
    contains_antigen: bool
    contains_enzyme: bool

    def pdb_path(self, pdb_name: str) -> str:
        """Constructs the relative path for a given PDB file within the Pinder dataset.

        Parameters:
            pdb_name (str): The name of the PDB file.

        Returns:
            str: The relative path as a string.
        """
        if pdb_name == "":
            return ""
        if self.test_system and (
            pdb_name.endswith("-R.pdb") or pdb_name.endswith("-L.pdb")
        ):
            pdbs_dir = "test_set_pdbs"
        else:
            pdbs_dir = "pdbs"
        return f"{pdbs_dir}/{pdb_name}"

    def mapping_path(self, pdb_name: str) -> str:
        if pdb_name == "":
            return ""
        return f"mappings/{pdb_name.replace('.pdb', '.parquet')}"

    @property
    def pdb_paths(self) -> dict[str, str | list[str]]:
        """dict[str, str | list[str]]: Dictionary containing the PDB type as key and PDB file name as value. Alternative apo monomers (if available) are returned as a list."""
        return {
            "native": self.pdb_path(self.pinder_pdb),
            "holo_R": self.pdb_path(self.holo_R_pdb),
            "holo_L": self.pdb_path(self.holo_L_pdb),
            "predicted_R": self.pdb_path(self.predicted_R_pdb),
            "predicted_L": self.pdb_path(self.predicted_L_pdb),
            "apo_R": self.pdb_path(self.apo_R_pdb),
            "apo_L": self.pdb_path(self.apo_L_pdb),
            "apo_R_alt": [
                self.pdb_path(p) for p in self.apo_R_alt if isinstance(p, str)
            ],
            "apo_L_alt": [
                self.pdb_path(p) for p in self.apo_L_alt if isinstance(p, str)
            ],
        }

    @property
    def mapping_paths(self) -> dict[str, str | list[str]]:
        """dict[str, str | list[str]]: Dictionary containing the PDB type as key and parquet file names corresponding to residue-level mapping information as value. are returned as a list."""
        return {
            "holo_R": self.mapping_path(self.holo_R_pdb),
            "holo_L": self.mapping_path(self.holo_L_pdb),
            "apo_R": self.mapping_path(self.apo_R_pdb),
            "apo_L": self.mapping_path(self.apo_L_pdb),
            "apo_R_alt": [
                self.mapping_path(p) for p in self.apo_R_alt if isinstance(p, str)
            ],
            "apo_L_alt": [
                self.mapping_path(p) for p in self.apo_L_alt if isinstance(p, str)
            ],
        }

    @property
    def pinder_id(self) -> str:
        """str: PINDER identifier for the dimer."""
        return self.id

    @property
    def pinder_pdb(self) -> str:
        """str: PINDER dimer PDB file name."""
        return self.id + ".pdb"

    @property
    def apo_R_alt(self) -> list[str] | list[None]:
        """list[str]: list of alternative apo receptor PDBs associated with entry."""
        return [f for f in self.apo_R_pdbs.split(";") if f != self.apo_R_pdb]

    @property
    def apo_L_alt(self) -> list[str] | list[None]:
        """list[str]: list of alternative apo ligand PDBs associated with entry."""
        return [f for f in self.apo_L_pdbs.split(";") if f != self.apo_L_pdb]

    @property
    def homodimer(self) -> bool:
        """bool: loose definition of whether the entry is a homodimer (based on identical receptor and ligand UniProt IDs)."""
        return self.uniprot_R == self.uniprot_L

    @property
    def test_system(self) -> bool:
        """bool: whether the system is part of the test split."""
        return self.split == "test"


class MetadataEntry(BaseModel):
    """Pydantic model representing a single entry in the Pinder metadata.

    Stores detailed metadata for a particular dataset entry as attributes.

    Parameters:
        id (str):
            The unique identifier for the PINDER entry.
            It follows the convention `<Receptor>--<Ligand>`, where `<Receptor>` is `<pdbid>__<chain_1>_<uniprotid>` and
            `<Ligand>` is `<pdbid>__<chain_2><uniprotid>`.
        entry_id (str):
            The RCSB entry identifier associated with the PINDER entry.
        method (str):
            The experimental method for structure determination (XRAY, CRYO-EM, etc.).
        date (str):
            Date of deposition into RCSB PDB.
        release_date (str):
